title: Computational methods for photoionization of H$_2$ molecules: a comparative study
authors: Hakon Volkmann, Jannis Schürmann, Alejandro Saenz
abstract: Single-photon ionization cross sections of molecular hydrogen in the electric dipole limit have been computed. Both time-dependent and -independent approaches within the clamped-nuclei approximation at equilibrium internuclear distance are employed, featuring the explicit time-propagation of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation and newly implemented multi-channel configuration-interaction free-boundary as well as complex-scaling methods using an explicitly correlated geminal basis set. The found results are compared to both experimental and previously published theoretical results, showing convincing mutual agreement despite their entirely different fundamental formulations. The novel CI-based approach demonstrates fast and controllable convergence while being able to provide full channel-resolved information.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive comparative study of computational methods used to calculate the single-photon ionization cross sections of molecular hydrogen. By applying time-dependent, time-independent, and complex-scaling techniques, the authors demonstrate strong agreement between fundamentally different theoretical formulations. This work provides robust validation for advanced quantum methods applied to molecular photoionization.
main_problem: The paper focuses on computing the single-photon ionization cross sections of molecular hydrogen ($	ext{H}_2$) in the electric dipole limit.
main_result: The computed results show convincing mutual agreement across multiple fundamentally different computational approaches (time-dependent vs. time-independent), validating the methods used.
method: A comparative study employing three main computational techniques: time-dependent Schrödinger equation propagation, time-independent free-boundary methods (CI-based), and complex-scaling geminal methods.
model_or_system: The physical system is the molecular hydrogen ($	ext{H}_2$) molecule, calculated at its equilibrium internuclear distance. The calculations utilize advanced electronic structure methods based on Configuration Interaction (CI) theory.
key_observables: Single-photon ionization cross sections ($\sigma$), ionization yield ($Y$), and optical oscillator strength (OOS) density.
important_parameters: Equilibrium internuclear distance ($R = 1.4 	ext{ a}_0$); the calculation is performed in the electric dipole limit.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions include the clamped-nuclei approximation and the use of various basis sets (e.g., B-splines) to discretize the continuum states.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the text references figures for high-energy computations and tables detailing CI configuration series.
paper_structure: The paper compares results from time-dependent, time-independent (Free-Boundary), and complex-scaling approaches to calculate the photoionization cross section, validating the consistency between these distinct theoretical formulations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it provides rigorous, comparative benchmarks for calculating fundamental molecular properties like photoionization cross sections using state-of-the-art quantum computational techniques.
